brief: NVDA posted a broad 3Q beat: EPS of $2.68 versus $2.48 consensus, revenue up 103% to $115.8bn versus $109.1bn consensus, driven by $107.6bn of data-center revenue, with gross margin of 74.9% above the 74.0% estimate. NVDA guided Q4 revenue to $126.1-133.9bn versus $125.25bn consensus and raised its FY2028 revenue growth outlook to roughly 75% from 70%, citing data-center readiness, durable demand and access to capital. Separately, UBS's 3Q26 earnings tracker shows 91.7% of S&P 500 market cap has reported, with blended estimates of 14.8% revenue growth and 32.8% EPS growth, and UBS's own running estimate at 33.0%. Growth is bifurcated by group: Energy leads at 155.2%, TECH+ at 50.7%, Cyclicals ex-Energy at 20.3%, Financials at 11.0%, Non-Cyclicals at 10.7%. Within TECH+, the six largest companies are expected to lag the rest of the market as a group (25.6% vs 35.2%); results are mixed, with META, MSFT, AAPL and NVDA beating their own estimates while GOOGL and AMZN missed. Aggregate earnings are beating by 5.8%, with 77% of companies topping estimates, and EPS revisions are improving atypically for this point in the season.
